questions.question: What is the primary non-renewable resource used to produce most traditional plastic food packaging?
options: Crude oil and other fossil fuels
Wood pulp from sustainable forests
Corn starch and plant oils
Natural gas liquids from renewable biogas

questions.question: Why is plastic waste in landfills and oceans considered a major environmental pollutant?
options: It dissolves quickly, making the water highly acidic.
It takes a very long time to degrade and can harm organisms.
It blocks all sunlight from reaching the deep ocean floor within days.
It releases large amounts of oxygen, causing fish populations to grow uncontrollably.

questions.question: Which of the following describes a sustainable alternative to traditional plastic packaging?
options: Metal-lined single-use foils
Chlorinated fluorocarbon wraps
Biodegradable bioplastics made from renewable resources
Heavy-duty synthetic polymer sheets

questions.question: What is one major benefit of using plastic packaging for fresh food products?
options: It completely eliminates the need for refrigeration during transport.
It helps prevent food spoilage and reduces food waste.
It increases the nutritional value of the food inside over time.
It accelerates the natural ripening process of fruits.

questions.question: When deciding whether to use plastic packaging for food, what trade-offs must we carefully weigh up?
options: The cost of the food versus the cost of the supermarket's electricity.
The weight of the food versus the distance it has to travel.
The benefits of reducing food waste against emissions from production and damage to biodiversity.
The color of the packaging against the amount of sugar in the food.

questions.question: What is one of the main human activities driving global deforestation?
options: Building solar farms in desert regions
Converting forested land for agricultural use
Collecting fallen branches for domestic heating
Extracting water from deep underground aquifers

questions.question: What is a direct consequence of deforestation on local wildlife?
options: An increase in available nesting sites
Improved adaptation to urban environments
Habitat loss for many different species
A rapid increase in genetic diversity

questions.question: How does converting natural land for agricultural use affect global ecosystems?
options: It increases the variety of wild animal species.
It is a major cause of habitat loss and biodiversity loss.
It helps wild plants grow faster by giving them more space.
It prevents soil erosion by introducing monoculture crops.

questions.question: Which of the following is a mitigation strategy used to restore lost ecosystems and protect biodiversity?
options: Increasing the use of chemical pesticides on all remaining forests
Positive land use changes, such as reforestation and rewilding
Converting national parks into urban residential zones
Encouraging a diet based entirely on imported processed foods

questions.question: Why is the future global supply of food considered to be at risk?
options: Due to the decreasing amount of carbon dioxide available for crops to grow
Because global warming and climate change threaten agricultural systems
Due to a worldwide shortage of synthetic packaging materials
Because plants are adapting to grow only in artificial greenhouses

questions.question: How do extreme weather events, made more common by climate change, affect farming?
options: They make it much easier to predict harvest times.
They reduce the need for artificial irrigation.
They make it more challenging to grow and produce food consistently.
They increase the natural fertility of agricultural soil worldwide.

questions.question: What contributes to the overall carbon footprint of the food we buy?
options: Only the breathing of the consumers who buy the food
The greenhouse gas emissions produced at various stages of food production
Only the electricity used by the checkout till at the supermarket
The amount of nitrogen gas absorbed by the food during cooking

questions.question: How can individual consumers help reduce greenhouse gas emissions associated with food production?
options: By eating more imported out-of-season foods
By making changes to our diets to choose foods with lower environmental impacts
By cooking all foods for twice as long to destroy carbon compounds
By replacing fresh water with carbonated drinks

questions.question: Why does cutting down forests disrupt the Earth's carbon cycle?
options: Fewer trees mean less carbon dioxide is absorbed from the atmosphere for photosynthesis.
It stops plants from releasing carbon dioxide through respiration.
It increases the rate at which plants convert nitrogen into carbon.
It causes the soil to absorb twice as much carbon dioxide as before.

questions.question: What is the role of carbon dioxide (CO2) in the atmosphere regarding global temperatures?
options: It reflects all solar radiation back into deep space, cooling the Earth.
It is a greenhouse gas that enhances the greenhouse effect and contributes to climate change.
It breaks down the ozone layer to allow cold polar winds to escape.
It blocks heat from leaving the oceans, causing tides to stop.

questions.question: How does deforestation affect the movement of water through the water cycle?
options: It increases the overall humidity of the local atmosphere.
It disrupts the cycle because fewer trees are absorbing and transpiring water.
It prevents rain from falling directly onto the soil.
It forces clouds to move faster across the land.

questions.question: Why does clearing forests increase the risk of flooding and threaten food security?
options: It causes rivers to dry up instantly, leaving no water for crops.
It leads to more surface runoff of water, which can flood farmland and ruin crops.
It increases the amount of groundwater stored in deep underground reservoirs.
It prevents any rain from falling on agricultural fields.

questions.question: What is the primary cause of modern global warming and climate change?
options: Natural variations in the distance between the Earth and the Moon
Human emissions of greenhouse gases into the atmosphere
Heat released from the core of the Earth through volcanic activity
An increase in the amount of dust entering the atmosphere from space

questions.question: Why does climate change present a survival challenge for many wild species?
options: It alters habitat conditions, meaning species may no longer be well adapted to live there.
It makes all habitats completely identical to one another.
It causes animals to lose their ability to reproduce permanently.
It increases the gravity in their local ecosystems.

questions.question: How can climate change and more frequent extreme weather events directly impact ecosystems?
options: They lead to a rapid increase in the number of new species being born.
They can lead to a significant loss of biodiversity.
They make ecosystems entirely immune to human activities.
They prevent any natural selection from occurring.
